title: English Rewind - 6 Minute English: Difficult pronunciation
speaker: BBC Learning English
zh: 【BBC Learning English】英語倒帶 - 6 分鐘英語：困難發音（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Hello! Catherine here from BBC Learning English.
cues.en: Hello! Catherine here from BBC Learning English.
cues.zh: 你好！來自 BBC 學習英語的凱瑟琳。

cues.text: Just so you know, this programme is from the BBC Learning English archive.
cues.en: Just so you know, this programme is from the BBC Learning English archive.
cues.zh: 如您所知，該程式來自 BBC Learning English 檔案。

cues.text: It was originally broadcast in October 2008 on our website.
cues.en: It was originally broadcast in October 2008 on our website.
cues.zh: 它最初於 2008 年 10 月在我們的網站上播出。

cues.text: We hope you enjoy it.
cues.en: We hope you enjoy it.
cues.zh: 我們希望您喜歡它。

cues.text: Hi, this is 6 Minute English and I'm Yvonne Archer.
cues.en: Hi, this is 6 Minute English and I'm Yvonne Archer.
cues.zh: 大家好，這裡是 6 分鐘英語，我是 Yvonne Archer。

cues.text: I'm Callum Robertson. Hello!
cues.en: I'm Callum Robertson. Hello!
cues.zh: 我是卡勒姆·羅伯森。你好！

cues.text: Hello, Callum.
cues.en: Hello, Callum.
cues.zh: 你好，卡勒姆。

cues.text: In this week's programme, English words that are often 'mispronounced'.
cues.en: In this week's programme, English words that are often 'mispronounced'.
cues.zh: 在本週的節目中，經常「讀錯」的英文單字。

cues.text: Callum, can you explain 'mispronounced' for us?
cues.en: Callum, can you explain 'mispronounced' for us?
cues.zh: 卡勒姆，你能為我們解釋一下「發音錯誤」嗎？

cues.text: Certainly. If you 'misprononce', if you 'mispronounce' a word,
cues.en: Certainly. If you 'misprononce', if you 'mispronounce' a word,
cues.zh: 當然。如果你“發音錯誤”，如果你“發音錯誤”一個單詞，

cues.text: you don't say it correctly.
cues.en: you don't say it correctly.
cues.zh: 你說得不對。

cues.text: You get some of the sounds wrong in that word.
cues.en: You get some of the sounds wrong in that word.
cues.zh: 你在這個詞中的一些發音是錯誤的。

cues.text: Very good. And is there a word that you often mispronounce, Callum?
cues.en: Very good. And is there a word that you often mispronounce, Callum?
cues.zh: 非常好。卡勒姆，有一個你常常讀錯的字嗎？

cues.text: Um, no, not really.
cues.en: Um, no, not really.
cues.zh: 嗯，不，不是真的。

cues.text: I didn't think so!
cues.en: I didn't think so!
cues.zh: 我不這麼認為！

cues.text: So I've got three difficult ones here for you!
cues.en: So I've got three difficult ones here for you!
cues.zh: 所以我這裡給你準備了三個困難的問題！

cues.text: But, before you read them out, any thoughts?
cues.en: But, before you read them out, any thoughts?
cues.zh: 但是，在你讀出它們之前，有什麼想法嗎？

cues.text: Well, looking at these words on paper, I think there's a good chance that some people would mispronounce them, yeah.
cues.en: Well, looking at these words on paper, I think there's a good chance that some people would mispronounce them, yeah.
cues.zh: 嗯，看看紙上的這些單詞，我認為有些人很可能會讀錯它們，是的。

cues.text: And that's why you're saying them instead of me! So, off you go.
cues.en: And that's why you're saying them instead of me! So, off you go.
cues.zh: 這就是為什麼你說的是他們而不是我！那麼，你走吧。

cues.text: OK, the words are: 'regularly', 'ethnicity' and 'anaesthetist'.
cues.en: OK, the words are: 'regularly', 'ethnicity' and 'anaesthetist'.
cues.zh: 好的，這些字是：「定期」、「種族」和「麻醉師」。

cues.text: Whew! Yeah, but you said them slowly, Callum!
cues.en: Whew! Yeah, but you said them slowly, Callum!
cues.zh: 哇！是的，但你說得很慢，卡勒姆！

cues.text: Yeah, that was tough.
cues.en: Yeah, that was tough.
cues.zh: 是的，那很艱難。

cues.text: But there are 3,000 other Brits who also agree that those words are difficult to say.
cues.en: But there are 3,000 other Brits who also agree that those words are difficult to say.
cues.zh: 但還有 3,000 名其他英國人也同意這些話很難說。

cues.text: They were recently questioned by a company called SpinVox and the research showed that 'regularly', 'ethnicity' and 'anaesthetist' —
cues.en: They were recently questioned by a company called SpinVox and the research showed that 'regularly', 'ethnicity' and 'anaesthetist' —
cues.zh: 他們最近受到一家名為 SpinVox 的公司的詢問，研究表明「經常」、「種族」和「麻醉師」——

cues.text: ooh, I said it! — are some of the most mispronounced words in the English language.
cues.en: ooh, I said it! — are some of the most mispronounced words in the English language.
cues.zh: 哦哦，我說了！ - 是英文中一些最容易發音錯誤的單字。

cues.text: Now before we hear more about that research, I've a question for you, Callum.
cues.en: Now before we hear more about that research, I've a question for you, Callum.
cues.zh: 現在，在我們瞭解更多有關該研究的資訊之前，我有一個問題要問你，卡勒姆。

cues.text: How many sounds do experts say we need to be able to pronounce,
cues.en: How many sounds do experts say we need to be able to pronounce,
cues.zh: 專家說我們需要能夠發音多少種聲音，

cues.text: so that we can speak English clearly? Is it a) 44? b) 104? Or 400?
cues.en: so that we can speak English clearly? Is it a) 44? b) 104? Or 400?
cues.zh: 以便我們能說清楚英語？是a）44嗎？ b) 104？還是400？

cues.text: Well, I'm fairly confident on this as I've just made a series on pronunciation.
cues.en: Well, I'm fairly confident on this as I've just made a series on pronunciation.
cues.zh: 嗯，我對此相當有信心，因為我剛剛做了一個關於發音的系列。

cues.text: In British English, there's generally about 44 sounds that are needed to pronounce English words.
cues.en: In British English, there's generally about 44 sounds that are needed to pronounce English words.
cues.zh: 在英式英語中，通常需要大約 44 個發音來發音英語單字。

cues.text: So, about 44, it's maybe a few more, but 44, that's my answer.
cues.en: So, about 44, it's maybe a few more, but 44, that's my answer.
cues.zh: 所以，大約44，可能還多一些，但44，這就是我的答案。

cues.text: Well, I'm not telling you! You'll have to wait until the end of the programme.
cues.en: Well, I'm not telling you! You'll have to wait until the end of the programme.
cues.zh: 好吧，我不告訴你！您必須等到節目結束。

cues.text: Now as we hear an extract from the BBC's Today programme on the most mispronounced words in English,
cues.en: Now as we hear an extract from the BBC's Today programme on the most mispronounced words in English,
cues.zh: 現在，當我們聽到 BBC 今日節目中關於英語中最容易發音錯誤的單字的摘錄時，

cues.text: try to find — whew, I can't pronounce 'try'!
cues.en: try to find — whew, I can't pronounce 'try'!
cues.zh: 試著找——哇，我發不出「嘗試」的音！

cues.text: Try to find out which word was the most mispronounced.
cues.en: Try to find out which word was the most mispronounced.
cues.zh: 試著找出哪個單字發音最錯誤。

cues.text: If you find 'statistics' and 'ethnicity' difficult to pronounce,
cues.en: If you find 'statistics' and 'ethnicity' difficult to pronounce,
cues.zh: 如果您發現“統計”和“種族”很難發音，

cues.text: it appears you're not alone.
cues.en: it appears you're not alone.
cues.zh: 看來你並不孤單。

cues.text: The Daily Mail says they're among the top ten most troublesome words in the English language.
cues.en: The Daily Mail says they're among the top ten most troublesome words in the English language.
cues.zh: 《每日郵報》稱它們是英文中十大最麻煩的單字之一。

cues.text: Researchers who questioned 3,000 people found that the most mispronounced word
cues.en: Researchers who questioned 3,000 people found that the most mispronounced word
cues.zh: 研究人員對 3000 人進行了詢問，發現發音最錯誤的單字是

cues.text: was 'phenomenon', followed by 'anaesthetist'.
cues.en: was 'phenomenon', followed by 'anaesthetist'.
cues.zh: 是“現象”，其次是“麻醉師”。

cues.text: Anaesthetist.
cues.en: Anaesthetist.
cues.zh: 麻醉師。

cues.text: And 'remuneration'.
cues.en: And 'remuneration'.
cues.zh: 還有‘報酬’。

cues.text: Callum, which word was the most troublesome, the most difficult to pronounce?
cues.en: Callum, which word was the most troublesome, the most difficult to pronounce?
cues.zh: Callum，哪個字最麻煩、最難發音？

cues.text: Well, that was 'phenomenon'. Phenomenon.
cues.en: Well, that was 'phenomenon'. Phenomenon.
cues.zh: 嗯，這就是「現象」。現象。

cues.text: Phenomenon? Phenomenon.
cues.en: Phenomenon? Phenomenon.
cues.zh: 現象？現象。

cues.text: Yep, I have to say, I have to take that one really slowly and just looking at it on paper makes me nervous.
cues.en: Yep, I have to say, I have to take that one really slowly and just looking at it on paper makes me nervous.
cues.zh: 是的，我必須說，我必須慢慢地做這個，光是看著紙上的內容就讓我感到緊張。

cues.text: So why do you think so many of us get it wrong, Callum?
cues.en: So why do you think so many of us get it wrong, Callum?
cues.zh: 那你認為為什麼我們很多人都搞錯了呢，卡勒姆？

cues.text: Well, of course, when we get nervous, we generally make more mistakes,
cues.en: Well, of course, when we get nervous, we generally make more mistakes,
cues.zh: 嗯，當然，當我們緊張的時候，我們通常會犯更多的錯誤，

cues.text: but here, it's the mixture of the particular sounds that are in words,
cues.en: but here, it's the mixture of the particular sounds that are in words,
cues.zh: 但在這裡，它是單字中特定聲音的混合，

cues.text: that's what causes the problems.
cues.en: that's what causes the problems.
cues.zh: 這就是造成問題的原因。

cues.text: So having the 'm' and 'n' sounds — the 'mm' and 'nn' in 'phenomenon' —
cues.en: So having the 'm' and 'n' sounds — the 'mm' and 'nn' in 'phenomenon' —
cues.zh: 所以有「m」和「n」的聲音——「現象」中的「mm」和「nn」——

cues.text: having so many of them so close together, that makes it a difficult word to pronounce.
cues.en: having so many of them so close together, that makes it a difficult word to pronounce.
cues.zh: 由於它們如此之多，距離如此之近，這使得它成為一個很難發音的單字。

cues.text: Mm, and what about 'anaesthetist'?
cues.en: Mm, and what about 'anaesthetist'?
cues.zh: 嗯，「麻醉師」呢？

cues.text: Well, 'anaesthetist', it contains an odd mixture of 't' and 'th' sounds.
cues.en: Well, 'anaesthetist', it contains an odd mixture of 't' and 'th' sounds.
cues.zh: 嗯，“anaesthetist”，它包含“t”和“th”聲音的奇怪混合。

cues.text: There's also an 's' in there as well, before that group of consonants
cues.en: There's also an 's' in there as well, before that group of consonants
cues.zh: 在那組子音之前還有一個“s”

cues.text: and that also makes things difficult to pronounce.
cues.en: and that also makes things difficult to pronounce.
cues.zh: 這也使得發音變得困難。

cues.text: Oh, dear, it certainly is!
cues.en: Oh, dear, it certainly is!
cues.zh: 噢，親愛的，當然是這樣！

cues.text: BBC Learning English dot com.
cues.en: BBC Learning English dot com.
cues.zh: BBC 學習英語 .com。

cues.text: Now, the newspaper that published those research results described such words as 'tongue-twisters'.
cues.en: Now, the newspaper that published those research results described such words as 'tongue-twisters'.
cues.zh: 現在，發表這些研究結果的報紙將這些詞形容為「繞口令」。

cues.text: But I wouldn't call them tongue-twisters, really, would you, Callum?
cues.en: But I wouldn't call them tongue-twisters, really, would you, Callum?
cues.zh: 但我不會稱它們為繞口令，真的嗎，卡勒姆？

cues.text: Not really, no, because 'tongue-twisters' are generally a sentence or an expression
cues.en: Not really, no, because 'tongue-twisters' are generally a sentence or an expression
cues.zh: 不是真的，不是，因為「繞口令」通常是一個句子或一個表達

cues.text: that is very difficult to say quickly and repeat again and again and again.
cues.en: that is very difficult to say quickly and repeat again and again and again.
cues.zh: 這很難快速說出來並一次又一次地重複。

cues.text: Well, I'm feeling really mean today, Callum.
cues.en: Well, I'm feeling really mean today, Callum.
cues.zh: 嗯，我今天感覺很不好，卡勒姆。

cues.text: Go on, give us an example and don't say it slowly!
cues.en: Go on, give us an example and don't say it slowly!
cues.zh: 來來來，給我們舉個例子，還不慢說！

cues.text: OK, try this one, A very famous one is
cues.en: OK, try this one, A very famous one is
cues.zh: 好的，試試這個，一個很有名的就是

cues.text: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled pepper." Cor, that was pretty good, wasn't it?!
cues.en: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled pepper." Cor, that was pretty good, wasn't it?!
cues.zh: 「彼得派珀摘了一小撮泡椒。」Cor，那很好，不是嗎？

cues.text: Of course, but we don't have to say tongue-twisters in life.
cues.en: Of course, but we don't have to say tongue-twisters in life.
cues.zh: 當然可以，但人生我們沒必要說繞口令。

cues.text: No.
cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.text: But we usually do have to use words like, what, 'statistics' and 'February'.
cues.en: But we usually do have to use words like, what, 'statistics' and 'February'.
cues.zh: 但我們通常必須使用「什麼」、「統計」和「二月」等字眼。

cues.text: I can't even say it myself, February.
cues.en: I can't even say it myself, February.
cues.zh: 我甚至不能自己說，二月。

cues.text: Well, yes. It is difficult to get through life without saying words like 'February'.
cues.en: Well, yes. It is difficult to get through life without saying words like 'February'.
cues.zh: 嗯，是的。如果不說「二月」這樣的詞，就很難度過一生。

cues.text: Yes. Mm.
cues.en: Yes. Mm.
cues.zh: 是的。毫米。

cues.text: But the research shows that many of us try to do just that.
cues.en: But the research shows that many of us try to do just that.
cues.zh: 但研究表明，我們中的許多人都試圖這樣做。

cues.text: We don't want to feel embarrassed when we mispronounce those words, so we just avoid them and that's a really bad example for learners, isn't it?
cues.en: We don't want to feel embarrassed when we mispronounce those words, so we just avoid them and that's a really bad example for learners, isn't it?
cues.zh: 我們不想在發音錯誤時感到尷尬，所以我們就避免使用它們，這對學習者來說是一個非常糟糕的例子，不是嗎？

cues.text: Well, I don't know about that. It's something natural that native speakers do.
cues.en: Well, I don't know about that. It's something natural that native speakers do.
cues.zh: 嗯，我對此一無所知。這是母語人士所做的很自然的事。

cues.text: That, you know, if you're not sure how to pronounce a word, choose another word or... And I do the same in writing, in spelling.
cues.en: That, you know, if you're not sure how to pronounce a word, choose another word or... And I do the same in writing, in spelling.
cues.zh: 那，你知道，如果你不確定如何發音一個單詞，請選擇另一個單詞或......我在寫作和拼寫方面也這樣做。

cues.text: If there's a word that I'm not sure how to spell, and my spelling isn't, you know, perfect,
cues.en: If there's a word that I'm not sure how to spell, and my spelling isn't, you know, perfect,
cues.zh: 如果有一個詞我不確定如何拼寫，而且我的拼寫也不是完美的，

cues.text: sometimes I will rewrite to avoid using that word.
cues.en: sometimes I will rewrite to avoid using that word.
cues.zh: 有時我會重寫以避免使用這個字。

cues.text: So, as in anything, pronunciation does only get better with practice,
cues.en: So, as in anything, pronunciation does only get better with practice,
cues.zh: 所以，就像任何事情一樣，發音只有透過練習才能變得更好，

cues.text: so don't worry about it!
cues.en: so don't worry about it!
cues.zh: 所以不用擔心！

cues.text: Just go for it. Mm.
cues.en: Just go for it. Mm.
cues.zh: 就去做吧。毫米。

cues.text: OK, now for the answer to our question.
cues.en: OK, now for the answer to our question.
cues.zh: 好的，現在回答我們的問題。

cues.text: How many sounds do experts say we need to be able to pronounce, so that we can speak English clearly?
cues.en: How many sounds do experts say we need to be able to pronounce, so that we can speak English clearly?
cues.zh: 專家說我們需要能夠發音多少種聲音，才能說清楚英語？

cues.text: Well, as I said, 44, I'm fairly confident that it's 44 or thereabouts.
cues.en: Well, as I said, 44, I'm fairly confident that it's 44 or thereabouts.
cues.zh: 嗯，正如我所說，44，我相當有信心它是 44 左右。

cues.text: Ah, you knew it all the time, Callum.
cues.en: Ah, you knew it all the time, Callum.
cues.zh: 啊，你一直都知道，卡勒姆。

cues.text: Well, that's all we've got time for today.
cues.en: Well, that's all we've got time for today.
cues.zh: 好了，我們今天的時間就到此為止。

cues.text: Join us again next time for more 6 Minute English.
cues.en: Join us again next time for more 6 Minute English.
cues.zh: 下次再加入我們，觀看更多 6 分鐘英語。

cues.text: Goodbye.
cues.en: Goodbye.
cues.zh: 再見。

cues.text: BBC Learning English dot com.
cues.en: BBC Learning English dot com.
cues.zh: BBC 學習英語 .com。
